title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor of Economics (Macroeconomics)
description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor of Economics
(Macroeconomics)
Washington and Lee University: Economics

Location: Lexington, VA
Open Date: Aug 31, 2026
Deadline:

Description
The Department of Economics in the Williams School of Commerce,
Economics, and Politics at Washington and Lee University invites
applications from candidates with teaching and research interests
in macroeconomics for a tenure-track position at the rank of
assistant professor of Economics. The appointment will begin July
1, 2027.

The successful candidate will teach the department's required
macroeconomics courses (Principles of Macroeconomics and
Macroeconomic Theory) and develop electives that build on existing
departmental strengths while expanding opportunities for
students.

Washington and Lee University is a highly selective, private,
liberal arts college, located in Lexington, VA (population 7,000).
W&L's Economics department offers an undergraduate major in
Economics and supports interdisciplinary minors in Africana
Studies; Data Science; Education Studies; Environmental Studies;
Law, Justice & Society; Middle East & South Asian Studies;
Poverty & Human Capability; and Women, Gender & Sexuality
Studies.

This position requires a strong commitment to excellence in
teaching within an undergraduate liberal arts setting. Candidates
should demonstrate the capacity to publish high-quality scholarly
research. The university supports faculty research through a
generous five-year sabbatical cycle, a pre-tenure research leave
program, opportunities for summer salary support, travel stipends,
and paid undergraduate research assistants. The department also
hosts a seminar series that meets regularly throughout the academic
year and features internal and external speakers.

The school calendar consists of two 13-week terms, one in the fall
and one in the winter, along with our unique 4-week spring term.
The regular teaching load is five courses per year. New hires teach
a 2-2-0 load in their first year to provide an opportunity to fully
participate in W&L's New Faculty Cohort, a comprehensive,
year-long faculty development program.

Washington and Lee University promotes a dynamic and welcoming
environment that allows students and employees of multiple
backgrounds and perspectives to learn, work, and thrive together.
Successful candidates will contribute to that environment and
exhibit potential for excellence in teaching and for rigorous
scholarship. We welcome applications from candidates who would
contribute to the University's mission and strategic plan.

The expected salary for this position is between $112,000-
$118,000. Offers are based on factors such as relevant education,
experience, tenure status, internal equity, and market and
organizational considerations.

Washington and Lee University offers a generous and comprehensive
benefits package designed to support the well-being of employees
and their families, as well as substantial support for faculty
development through research funding, a strong culture of
mentorship, and a pre-tenure leave program. To learn more about
working at W&L, employee benefits, and life in the Shenandoah
Valley, visit jobs.wlu.edu.




Qualifications
A Ph.D. in Economics is required by the time of appointment.



Application Instructions
Review of applications will begin November 13, 2026. Candidates
should submit the following materials through the Interfolio portal
at https://apply.interfolio.com/192513:


Letter of Application summarizing your teaching interests and
experience, your interest in a liberal arts environment, your
scholarly contributions or plans, and your ability to work with
students with a broad range of backgrounds and experiences
CV
Evidence of Teaching Effectiveness including a teaching
statement, representative syllabi (if applicable), list of courses
taught, and course evaluations (please note: "Selected comments"
are not considered a substitute for full course evaluations)
Three confidential letters of recommendation
Job Market Paper



If you have questions about the position, please contact Katie
Shester, chair of the search committee, at shesterk@wlu.edu.



For more information and to apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/192513


Washington and Lee is an Equal Opportunity Employer
seeking candidates committed to high standards of scholarship,
performance, professionalism, and to a welcoming campus community.
Job description requirements are representative, but not
all‐inclusive of the knowledge, skill, and abilities needed to
successfully perform this job. Reasonable accommodations may be
made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform
essential functions.
